artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Dudt was convicted and suspended from office by the Midway Presbyterian Church Session for emailing the congregation an SJC decision and expressing disagreement with a Session action, which the Session characterized as violating his ordination vows. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversing in whole and rendering a verdict of not guilty, finding that the Session had no constitutional authority to forbid Dudt from distributing the SJC decision and that the charges of false statements were not proven. A concurring opinion by several judges cautioned against elders emailing congregations in disagreement with Session decisions.

artifacts.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the complaint, ruling that a Session erred by prescreening and eliminating a deacon's nomination for ruling elder before the mandatory instruction and examination process required by BCO 24-1. The decision held that BCO 24-1's language is mandatory and that sessions cannot add a preliminary vetting step that bypasses the required sequence of instruction and examination.

artifacts.title: Dodson et al. v. Ohio Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

artifacts.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE Evans under BCO 38-1 without properly securing his approval of the full statement of facts, as the Investigative Committee's report added additional adverse facts he had not seen or approved. The SJC sustained the complaints of Evans and Pitts et al., annulled the deposition, and remanded the matter to AZP for action consistent with BCO 38-1 requirements; a lengthy concurring opinion by RE Donahoe extensively analyzed BCO 38-1 confession procedures.

artifacts.title: Fozard v. North Texas Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Chandler Fozard complained that Fort Worth Presbyterian Church's policy restricting the integration of special case felons (including sex offenders) into the congregation violated Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint 20-1, finding the complainant had not demonstrated the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution, while criticizing the Session's arguments from BCO Preliminary Principles 1 and 2 as improper.

artifacts.title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Frazier complained that Nashville Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Scott Sauls regarding his teaching on same-sex attraction; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0-1, concluding NP fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties, accompanied by several concurring opinions raising procedural and exegetical concerns.

artifacts.title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley
artifacts.synopsis: Bumgarner, a ruling elder who had been deposed in 2012, filed a BCO 40-5 application in 2015 seeking reversal of the censure after having previously withdrawn his complaint and acknowledged it could not be resubmitted. The SJC dismissed the application as administratively out of order because it sought to re-file a withdrawn complaint and because BCO 40-3 prohibits reversal of judicial censures except by appeal or complaint.

artifacts.synopsis: TE John Hardie appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Metro Atlanta Presbytery's judicial commission, raising seventeen specifications of error under six categories including procedural irregularities, improper evidence, refusal of indulgence, prejudice, and disproportionate censure. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error in MAP's proceedings and upholding the indefinite suspension.

artifacts.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.
